\section[a exceção]{a exceção — the exception}

\label{lesson:PT-C383-excecao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to break, then the Portuguese for the violation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a exceção}
\textbf{a exceção} — \textquotedblleft{}the exception\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Todos pagam, sem exceção.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Everyone pays, without exception.}
\end{quote}

AO90 \emph{exceção}; older \emph{excepção}. \emph{Abrir uma exceção} — to make an exception.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{exceção} comes from Latin \emph{exceptiō} \textquotedblleft{}an exception, a restriction\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), on \emph{excipere} \textquotedblleft{}to take out\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{capere} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a exceção}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a exceção}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a exceção}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to break, then the Portuguese for the violation, then say \emph{a exceção} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a exceção mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The exception\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o requisito]{o requisito — the requirement}

\label{lesson:PT-C383-requisito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the violation, then the Portuguese for the exception.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o requisito}
\textbf{o requisito} — \textquotedblleft{}the requirement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Falar inglês é um requisito para este trabalho.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Speaking English is a requirement for this job.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Cumprir os requisitos} — to meet the requirements.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{requisito} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{requīsītus} \textquotedblleft{}required, sought\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), the participle of \emph{requīrere}, built on \emph{quaerere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[excluir]{excluir — to exclude, to leave out; to rule out}

\label{lesson:PT-C383-excluir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the exception, then the Portuguese for the requirement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: excluir}
\textbf{excluir} — \textquotedblleft{}to exclude, to leave out; to rule out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não excluo a hipótese de mudar de casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not rule out the possibility of moving house.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated like \emph{concluir}: \emph{excluo, excluis, exclui}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{excluir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{exclūdere} \textquotedblleft{}to shut out, to exclude\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{ex} and \emph{claudere} \textquotedblleft{}to shut\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a infração]{a infração — the offence, the infringement (of a rule)}

\label{lesson:PT-C383-infracao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the requirement, then the Portuguese for to exclude.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a infração}
\textbf{a infração} — \textquotedblleft{}the offence, the infringement (of a rule)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Estacionar ali é uma infração.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Parking there is an offence.}
\end{quote}

AO90 \emph{infração}; older \emph{infracção}. \emph{Infração de trânsito} — traffic offence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{infração} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{īnfrāctiō} \textquotedblleft{}a breaking\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{īnfringere} \textquotedblleft{}to break, to infringe\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{frangere} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[transgredir]{transgredir — to transgress, to break (a rule)}

\label{lesson:PT-C383-transgredir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to exclude, then the Portuguese for the offence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: transgredir}
\textbf{transgredir} — \textquotedblleft{}to transgress, to break (a rule)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Quem transgride as regras paga uma multa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Whoever breaks the rules pays a fine.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated like \emph{agredir}: \emph{transgrido, transgrides, transgride}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{transgredir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{trānsgredī} \textquotedblleft{}to step across, to pass over\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{trāns} \textquotedblleft{}across\textquotedblright{} and \emph{gradī} \textquotedblleft{}to step\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
